spec_summary: In-browser EPUB reader for RetroShelf; no-JS, old-iPad compatible; quality 34/35
shared_context:
## Meta
Project: RetroShelf (Kavita-Retro-iPad) — repo /home/caleb/Projects/Kavita-Retro-iPad.
Spec: docs/specs/2026-08-23-epub-reader.md (quality 34/35). Design: docs/plans/2026-08-23-epub-reader-design.md.

## Context
RetroShelf is a server-rendered, ZERO-JavaScript FastAPI + Jinja2 bridge that proxies
OPDS libraries to iOS 5.1.1-12 Safari and hands books to iBooks with exact headers.
This spec adds an in-browser EPUB reader on the same constraints.
Patterns to follow: capped reads (app/kavita.py KavitaClient._read_capped), temp-file +
os.replace atomic writes (app/download.py cover cache, app/store.py Store._save), typed
errors via RetroShelfError subclass + app/main.py _ERROR_TABLE row, record projection
(app/store.py sanitize_record), bridge ids via app/main.py _record_id, image type
validation (app/download.py _safe_image_type), Sphinx docstrings, mypy zero, ruff clean.

## Intent (trade-off hierarchy)
1. Old-Safari compatibility (no JS, no CSS Grid/flex, plain <a href> links) beats everything.
2. Correctness of the sanitizer seam beats performance.
3. Serve-path speed beats shelve-path speed.
4. Consistency with existing codebase patterns beats ideal design.
5. Simple beats flexible (YAGNI).
Escalate (stop, report PARTIAL) when: new runtime dependency needed; sanitizer cannot pass
a fixture without weakening attribute rules; existing download/header code paths need
modification; Store schema needs fields beyond the committed interface.

## Constraints
Musts: every upstream byte through KavitaClient.resolve_url; sanitize at shelve time;
`| safe` only on sanitizer output, once, commented; caps (80MB EPUB spooled to temp file,
500 spine, 2MB/chapter, 120MB unpacked, 1GB reader cache); atomic writes; no upstream URL
on disk; Sphinx docstrings; mypy zero; ruff clean.
Must-nots: NO JavaScript / CSS Grid / unprefixed-flex; NO changes to existing
download/cover/OPDS behavior or headers; NO credentialed URLs on disk or in HTML;
NO new runtime dependencies.

## Edge Cases
Malformed chapter -> escaped-text blocks; DRM -> ReaderError friendly page; oversize ->
ReaderError before exhaustion, spool cleaned; zip-slip rejected; cache pruned mid-book ->
transparent re-shelve; Pillow absent -> text-only; non-EPUB record on /read -> friendly 404;
zero readable chapters -> ReaderError; stalled upstream -> 120s bounded timeout; concurrent
shelve -> tmp-dir + rename idempotent; literal {IMG:0} in book text -> benign.

- Build: /home/caleb/Projects/Kavita-Retro-iPad/.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q app
- Test: /home/caleb/Projects/Kavita-Retro-iPad/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
- Types: /home/caleb/Projects/Kavita-Retro-iPad/.venv/bin/python -m mypy app
- Lint: /home/caleb/Projects/Kavita-Retro-iPad/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check app tests
Note: no start_command runtime verification needed — all [BEHAVIORAL]/[INTEGRATION]
criteria are exercised through pytest + FastAPI TestClient with mocked upstreams (this is
the project's established verification style; the suite IS the runtime harness).
